def: Certain to happen; impossible to avoid.
ex: With so many dark clouds, rain was inevitable.

def: To keep trying even when something is difficult.
ex: If you persevere, you'll master the guitar.

def: A difficult choice between two options.
ex: Choosing between the two clubs was a real dilemma.

def: Able to recover quickly from difficulties.
ex: Children are often more resilient than adults think.

def: An agreement where each side gives up something.
ex: We reached a compromise: one film each.

def: Paying great attention to every small detail.
ex: He's meticulous about painting his model planes.

def: To expect something and prepare for it.
ex: We didn't anticipate so many visitors.

def: Able to be understood in more than one way.
ex: The ending of the film is ambiguous.

def: Something that happens and can be seen, often unusual.
ex: The northern lights are an amazing natural phenomenon.

def: To grow or develop very well.
ex: These plants thrive in sunny places.

def: Causing a lot of disagreement.
ex: Homework at weekends is a controversial topic.

def: The ability to act on your own without being told.
ex: She showed initiative by organising the bake sale.

def: To give more details about something.
ex: Could you elaborate on your idea?

def: Not obvious; small but important.
ex: There's a subtle difference between the two colours.

def: Agreement among everyone in a group.
ex: The class reached a consensus about the trip.

def: Easily hurt or harmed.
ex: Baby turtles are vulnerable to hungry birds.

def: To show that something is especially important.
ex: The coach likes to emphasise teamwork.

def: Seeming likely to be true.
ex: His excuse sounded plausible, but nobody believed it.

def: Something that blocks your way or makes progress difficult.
ex: Fear of failure is the biggest obstacle.

def: Despite what has just been said.
ex: It was raining. Nevertheless, we enjoyed the walk.

def: Able to do many different things.
ex: A pencil is a surprisingly versatile tool.

def: To accept or admit that something is true.
ex: She had to acknowledge that the other team played better.

def: Clear and logical, with parts that fit together.
ex: Make sure your essay is coherent.

def: An unfair preference for or against someone or something.
ex: A good referee shows no bias.

def: To become or make something smaller or less.
ex: Nothing could diminish their excitement.

def: Possible and practical to do.
ex: Is it feasible to finish the model by Friday?

def: A possible effect or result of something.
ex: Think about the implication of skipping breakfast.

def: Very great or deep.
ex: The trip had a profound effect on her.

def: To publicly support an idea.
ex: Many doctors advocate eating more vegetables.

def: Careful to avoid danger or problems.
ex: Be cautious when crossing busy roads.

def: An idea or belief.
ex: The notion that all cats hate water isn't true.

def: Very great or strong, and hard to deal with.
ex: The response to our charity sale was overwhelming.

def: To examine something very carefully.
ex: The judges scrutinise every cake in the competition.

def: Careful to do your work well and thoroughly.
ex: She's a conscientious student who checks every answer.

def: Used to say something can be supported with good reasons.
ex: She is arguably the best player on the team.

def: Doubting that something is true.
ex: I'm sceptical about the story of a monster in the lake.

def: To make something weaker, often gradually.
ex: Constant teasing can undermine your confidence.

def: Happening in many places or among many people.
ex: There was widespread excitement about the eclipse.

def: To give a share of something for a particular purpose.
ex: The school will allocate more money to the library.

def: Including everything that is needed.
ex: The guidebook gives a comprehensive list of museums.
